title: 4th Sitting of third session of 2025

items.text: Opening recitation (Hamd and Salawat); the sitting begins.
Roll call of members present at the sitting.
Announcement of the day's agenda (Agenda No. އޖ/4/3/2025).
Approval of the minutes of four previous special sittings (minutes Nos. 4/ޚޞ/2025/20 to 7/ޚޞ/2025/20).

Written question by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister of Homeland Security and Technology Ali Ihusan: the Presidential Commission report on Hawwa Yumnu Rasheed, who fell from a building in Malé, found police negligence and recommended action; has any action been taken against any police personnel, and if so what?

Written question by Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim to Minister of Homeland Security and Technology Ali Ihusan: are the police criminally investigating those the Presidential Commission's report on the Hawwa Yumnu Rasheed case said should be investigated, and how far have those investigations progressed?
First reading of Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim's bill amending Law No. 8/2009 (Maldives Pension Act).
Preliminary debate on Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim's bill amending Law No. 4/2007 (Audit Act).
Preliminary debate on Galolhu North MP Mohamed Ibrahim's bill amending Law No. 3/2013 (Privatization, Corporatization, Monitoring and Evaluation of State Enterprises Act).

Continued debate on the resolution submitted by Madaveli MP Mohamed Shameez calling for the corruption flagged in the Auditor General's special audit report on Fenaka Corporation Limited to be investigated and acted on quickly.
Report of the Judiciary Committee on the President's submission to appoint 2 members to the Tax Appeal Tribunal under Article 56(a)(1) of Law No. 3/2010 (Tax Administration Act).
Voting on items from the day's business that have reached the voting stage.

summary: The sitting approved special-sitting minutes, put written questions on the Hawwa Yumnu Rasheed case, introduced a Pension Act amendment, opened debate on Audit Act and privatization amendments, continued the Fenaka resolution, and took a report on Tax Appeal Tribunal appointments.
